title: CVE-2026-110264: Critical GitLab RCE Flaw Affects 12 Years of Releases
content_md: GitLab has released urgent security updates addressing CVE-2026-110264, a maximum-severity vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on vulnerable self-managed GitLab servers. The flaw carries a CVSS score of 10.0 and affects both GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE). The vulnerability is particularly notable because the affected code dates back to GitLab 7.0, released in 2014. This leaves roughly 12 years of GitLab releases within the vulnerable range, although there is currently no evidence that attackers have been exploiting the weakness throughout that period. GitLab disclosed the issue and released patched versions on October 21, 2026. The vulnerability originates from an integer overflow triggered while GitLab compiles a specially crafted regular expression. Under certain conditions, an unauthenticated attacker could use that condition to execute arbitrary code on the underlying GitLab server. GitLab has intentionally withheld the complete exploitation path and specific prerequisites while administrators deploy patches. For organizations running self-managed GitLab infrastructure, the potential impact is severe. GitLab repositories frequently contain source code, CI/CD configuration, deployment secrets, access tokens, infrastructure definitions, and connections to production environments.
